title: The Harold Shipman Patient Murders
evidence: Medical records showed unusually high numbers of patient deaths
Toxicology identified lethal levels of diamorphine in victims
Shipman falsified medical records and death certificates
A forged will connected Shipman to the estate of victim Kathleen Grundy
The official Shipman Inquiry identified 215 unlawful killings and suspected 45 additional deaths
modus_operandi: Uses his position as a general practitioner to gain complete trust from patients. During home visits he administers lethal doses of diamorphine, records or reports a fabricated natural cause of death, and falsifies medical documentation to conceal the killings.
personality_disorder: No definitive clinical personality-disorder diagnosis should be assigned. The documented behavioral profile includes deception, manipulation, abuse of professional authority, falsification of records, and extreme exploitation of patient trust.
summary: British physician who murdered patients over decades by exploiting his position as a trusted doctor. The official inquiry concluded that he unlawfully killed 215 patients and found a real suspicion concerning 45 additional deaths.
